review_text: Very good professor, excels at explaining the concepts to students in basic terms and drawing insights from industry standards. Friendly and approachable.

His lectures are hard to listen to. Homework is easy but tests are horrible. They are also the main graded segments. Handwriting is legible but hard to read. Claims his class is easy because the topics are easy but does not teach as such. grades very lightly. I messed up on my midterm but he bumped it up a few. i dont feel like i learned. :[

Lectures are nothing more than reading slides (which are already awful and made by a different professor 5+ years ago) and his voice is so quiet that students have to ask him to speak up every class. Final was 30% of final grade, bloated with more questions so it's actually worth more than 30% in the end. SFSU Machine Structures is a scam course.

He's the only professor (not a lecturer) currently teaching CSC 220. An extremely experienced programmer, he incorporates plenty of live coding into his lectures, making it an excellent way to learn Java programming and data structures. He is vary caring and easy going. I highly recommend taking CSC 220 with him.

I believe 95% of the kids get either A/B in the course. Attendance quizzes, 6 homework assignments and a midterm and final are the majority of this class. If you have quarter of a brain you'll do fine.

mandatory lecture quizzes that you work on by urself then he shows how to solve.20% of grade. HW not long, 40% of grade. 2 Multiple choice exams 20% each. can explain anything. He is worth being your first option for professor. Low stress, good for people working or have other obligations in life

Good teacher! took him for 220, is very passionate about the subject and helps explain, has quizzes every class but don't worry he goes over it so its impossible to not get full points, homework assignments are easy to understand, midterms are based off quizzes he give during class. 10/10 professor would 100% take him again

Professor Akila fostered an environment where critical thinking and deeper understanding were valued. Challenging topics like recursion, linked lists, and trees were broken down into clear, digestible explanations with practical examples that connected theory to real-world applications.
One of the best professors I ever had.

Very good class, learned a lot and it's very easy to get a good grade if you lock in and participate in the lectures. Final/Midterm is multiple choice, making it so much better in comparison to the written CS tests, which made me understand the topics much better as I was able to focus rather than worry about the actual written code. GOATED
Took him for CSC 220, Data Structures. The old adage rings true, "those who can't do, teach." Avoid this professor at all costs.
great

I recently took CSC 665 with Professor Akila de Silva. He is not a tough grader. The course consist of assignments and quizzes making up 60% of the overall grade, followed by two midterms, each worth 10%, and a final exam worth 20%. Also, there was an optional mini-project that offered 10% extra credit, which was a great opportunity for students.

Took CS620 with this professor. I found the environment difficult for asking questions. When students sought clarification, she often responded with laughter rather than an explanation, which discouraged class participation. I'd recommend looking for a section that better fosters open discussion.

Takes things too personally, lacks professionalism. Teaches some concepts well and most concepts horribly. Outdated teaching practices. Hate the way she pronounces "matrices". Lecture slides are a mess, and she goes through them so fast. I uploaded all the slides onto ChatGPT to learn the material. Also, HW is irrelevant and not discussed at all.

Very difficult class as the lectures were not very helpful in the quizzes nor homework, and you are expected to learn on your own for most of the homework assignments. Her slides for class are also very confusing to look at (jumbled up, especially if you are trying to look at it before a quiz) and explanations are confusing as well.

Very impressive for a week and a half, then disappointments and more disappointments. She is very unorganized and apparently unprepared for the class. However, she preaches and blames it all on students. Her knowledge is very outdated. She is too busy with so many roles and offices she is holding. No time for teaching or students. Grading is awful.

A drama queen. She tries hard to be young and sweet. Her lectures are confusing. She tests on things she does not cover. Her assignments are totally outdated and irrelevant in some ways. It is to tell that she does not prepare for her lectures. She reads of the ppt slides and often loses track of what she is saying.

if you aren't good with attendance and showing up on time, don't sign up for this class. attendance, 12 weekly quizzes that are based on lectures, and 6 homework assignments are 90% of the class. The quizzes are somewhat tough but if you read the lectures you should be fine. The homework assignments are vague, so ask questions if you're confused.

She is very sweet and wants everyone to learn and succeed in the class, however, her lectures are not engaging; she reads from the slides and her explanations are vague.Quizes are kind of hard but if you learn the material you should do ok. Homework is outdated and sometimes difficult to understand so you do not really know what to do.

Easily one of the best professors. Her lectures are amazing and funnily enough, NLP is probably the best "intro to AI" course simply because she explains all the concepts so well. Attendance is mandatory and there are weekly quizzes based off the slides from the previous week. Do the work, attend class, and it's an easy A and you'll learn lots.
Professor Kulkarni is not a good pick for this class, unfortunately she is the only professor who teaches NLP at SFSU. I would rather take an online course from Coursera.
Very interesting lectures with a caring and respectful professor. Fun assignments but sometimes are a bit tedious due to some outdated packages to install and fix.
One of the most easy going professors at SFSU. You'll have fun learning from him if you are really interested in learning the art of Full stack development.
One of the best teachers I've had so far at SFSU. Highly recommend. Industry experience and wants students to succeed.

Professor Scott is one of the best computer science teachers I have ever had. His projects are straightforward and you will learn new things. Even when they get difficult, the solutions give you the necessary experience for software development projects. He is also accessible outside of class and very helpful.

Professor is very understanding and wants you to succeed. His class is straightforward and you just need to stay up with the work because doing projects last minute is almost a death sentence for your grade. I would recommend, if possible, to do the group projects with people you are familiar with and/or have good work ethic/ communication.

He's an excellent teacher, addressing all questions seriously. One semester entails three solo assignments and a group report, split into three parts. If your group remains active, it's not challenging. Earning points is straightforward, and extra credit is available. Achieving an A shouldn't be too difficult.
Extremely unreasonable grading
Best guy this side of the golden gate bridge

Prof Souza is amazing. I was terrified to take CSC and had a lot of preconceived notions about taking CSC, but all of those fears were shattered by how great a Prof he is. Every topic was presented in an understandable and digestible way. He treats every student with respect and truly wants to see you succeed. Def take his class.

Great professor. Took it in summer, lectures mainly focused on assignments and had recordings. Get ready to read, instructions of assignments are very long but not difficult. Always turned the lecture before assignment deadline into an optional lab session. Attendance as EC and also provided EC on assignments.
He is chill and understanding. His lectures are amazing. He makes us understand the materials easily. Take his class, you will not regret.

Don't take him unless you're unemployed and/or enrolled part-tine. That is where all his good reviews come from. Assignments have prompts up to 20 pages long, or more. And he doesn't prepare you for them at all. Allergic to teaching. Expects students to learn everything on their own. Does not approve W's or pass/no-pass. Hates his job and students.

This course is more about how much you put in. The class lectures were middle of the ground, most of the time it feels like hes just trying to take up time till he hits the end of class. Yeah its a easy course basically a free A. If you do everything and dont use AI you learn quite a bit, but can't say its due to him more so due to the projects.

Took his class over the summer, so it was a bit more accelerated, but the way he taught the material was good and I enjoyed his class overall. It was a solo project which I heard has been turned into a group project, so it was a bit more difficult but he was pretty lenient with the grading.

I don't understand his high rating. He gets very off-topic. I had to watch recordings of lectures even though I attended them. Applying the lectures to the homework is like searching for a needle in a haystack he is so off-topic. Also, I had a very serious injury preventing me from taking the final. He ghosted and failed me like a coward. Unreal!!!
Loved his csc101, felt like rather than straight up zombie coding I was actually learning something, it felt good and he was always there to answer questions.
Good Professor

He had absolutely no energy in any of his lessons it was very dry. If you don't have any previous CAD experience this class may be tough. He is rigorous on how you draft and present drawings, grades very harshly. I will give him the benefit of the doubt because it was an evening class, everyone wants to go home. He's a mediocre Professor.

Down to earth guy. Class can be dry at times. Tends to rush in presenting things on AutoCAD. Wish he would slow down so I can take notes on how to do certain things. Class is passable, you can show up and basically wing it. Homework is 30%. Drawing Assignmetns 60% and the final exam is 10%.

Get ready to learn nothing and struggle a lot. The projects instructions are so obscure, expect to get marked down for his inability to write good documents. He just reads from his written book in class. I think you should stay away from prof that writes their own book. They think they are hot stuff or something but they only read from this book.
One of the harder classes I have taken, but it was super rewarding. This class easily was one of the most homework intensive ones I took.

This guy barely teaches at all. All he does in class is "Read the book, chapter xxx and the reader, chapter xxx." He even combines two sections of class into one big class with more than 100 students. Worst professor ever.

The class was an awful experience. His lectures consists of him reading word for word from his laptop which is displayed on the projector. The last few projects (labeled milestones), contained such little information on how to implement the code that it took many hours of using ctrl-f in his 300 page course reader to even get an idea.

Absolutely horrible. His projects make no sense & take hours, & he barely gives you a week to do each project. For exams theres a study guide of 70 questions but he doesn't provide any answers so you have to figure everything out on your own. He gives no partial credit on assignments/exams. Harsh grading & all he does is read off his computer.

Assignments are time consuming and demanding, especially the later ones, but definitely hold value. His lectures are a bit of a pain; he goes through his reader on the projector, summing it up as he goes, which is worse than just reading it yourself. He is passionate about what he does though (teaching and his OpenMRS work). He is super kind.
Nice guy!
He's a knowledgeable teacher, but old fashioned and old schoolstyled.

I don't think Prof Levine is as bad as people make him out to be. His projects were long and tedious but you definitely learn a lot from them. Levine also gives good advice on CS career related things. His main downside is he can be a brutal grader on the exam and gives little hints as to what will be on them. Exams are like 60% of your grade too.

Definitely has to be the worst experience I've ever had with a teacher. Contradictory assignment guidelines, extremely harsh on grading, material presented extremely unprofessional. Slides and code are all word format, no syntax highlighting (as is the reader). Makes attendance mandatory but goes on tangents constantly. Go for another teacher!

2 homework assignments, 1 project, 1 final, and the class assignments. He goes over the class assignments with you during lecture, so if you're there or watch the lecture after, ez points. if you don't do well on homework assignments, the group project makes up for it. GET A GOOD GROUP. Final is automated grading, so do with that what you will.

Brian was such a great professor. Constantly giving feedback and always available for any questions or assistance. The course consisted of Weekly online meetings, 2 Homework assignments, 1 Final, 1 Group project. Pay attention in class, follow directions and you will easily pass.

Great professor, he very chill and understanding. While his lectures were a bit heavy, he would always do demos on the classwork and even go over the homework answers (after they are due). You turn in HW through GitHub which is auto graded, one exam, and a final group project. If you follow along and do the HW you should do fine.

Most reviews are true. His lecture very clear. The class not as hard but the homework might be challenge. He answer questions very details. Push code to gitHub and as long as you get the green check, you got full credit. Same as the homework assignments. Will take his other class in the future!

He is a great and kind professor. pushing the code to Git Hub every lecture is the participation score: 2H.W., 1 group project, and one final. Homework 1 was tough but you have a month to learn all you need and do it. homework 2 builds on H.w1 and the final project is similar to homework 2. Overall, put in the work and you will be fine.

You follow his lectures by copying the code he writes and submitting on GitHub, he also does review on stuff a week before homework is due. Two "big" homework assignments, given a month in advance, maybe he pushes back the due date. Final project is combination of homework and lectures. Felt disorganized but as long as you're on point it's an A.

He takes attendance by having you turn in classwork for every lecture. He is lecture heavy but very thorough. He will spend extra time on harder topics or if you ask questions. There's two solo projects and one group project, plus a final. He's very clear about his grading criteria, and he gave my entire class extra credit.

DON'T LISTEN TO THE OTHER REVIEWS. This class is really hard and the professor didn't make it any easier. the group project is unreasonable and the course it so time consuming. even tho it's online you will end up spending more time than you would with in-person class.

Good professor, he is chill and easy going. He is very patience and explain every part. His homework might be a little difficult, but once you get it, it is easy. His final project is not bad at all, you should have a easy course with him.

It was a hard course. Even though he gave us like a month to finish 1 hw assignment, it was still really difficult to keep up with the class. I def learned a lot from his class, but if you team up with crappy teammates for final project, you're basically on your own for a full-stack project. He gave out a lot of hints though.

Briana was an absolutely amazing teacher! I am not too good with speeches but the class went by quite smoothly because of how clear all of the assignments were. I would definitely take the class again.

She is very helpful. Her class is always fun. Participation matters the most. Constant engaging is very important. Questions of the day, attendance part is so fun. Very clear grading, gives good feedback. I definitely recommend to take her class. Easy A.
Best Comm Professor ever

Briana is a great teacher! She really cares about her students, treats them like friends and really tries to know ever single one, and really creates a great learning environment! There is some reading, a few worksheets, but the only hard work is working on speeches, which she gives lots of help with. Def. go to class, her lectures are worth it!
Brianna is a bad ass professor. She has awesome hair and really cares about her students. Definitely take this class with her.

Super nice and considerate of students. The teacher has fun happy energy. If want an easy A take this class. But do not miss any classes because attendence is a part of your grade. If you miss a class you must tell her asap otherwise she will not let you makeup for the work. Overall, I recommend .
Expect no homework/classwork. Only actual work you do is to write your short speeches. Easy A :)

homework 15%, 2 midterms are 20% each, final is 45%. He reads off slides that he has forever and first day just jumps in material. Majority of the class was not passing, if you have trouble with taking test this might not be the best teacher to take. Teacher looks half sleep trying to teach the class behind his tablet. Not enthusiastic.

Just be prepared to write long 5-10 page essays, not bad he gives you a lot of time to write them 3 essays total. The attendance isn't mandatory but do show up for the first three weeks of class so he doesn't drop you. There are quizzes that are short answer questions but there really is no wrong or right answer just justify why you chose it.
Not a really preferred professor. Definitely easy to get an A but lectures are boring.

Idk how anyone can hate him. The assignments are easy, attendance is optional as long as you show up to a few classes and participate in discussions, and he is actually a really chill guy. This class is an easy A and the professor is really smart and caring.
They just be letting anyone teach nowadays.. easy professor tho nothing really going on in class

Lectures are just reading handwritten notes on a projector and some confusing examples. Almost weekly homework's but they are only 15%, the rest of your grade is two midterms (40%) and a final (45%). Only 3-5 people showed up to lecture because the notes that are almost the entirety of the lecture are on canvas. Help yourself, take someone else!
I do not know how the university allows him to keep teaching. He should be enjoying retirement. Every lecture I was afraid he'd have a heart attack.

Professor is a nice guy yet he doesn't really teach well in my opinion. From day one he instantly jumps into the material with no explanation of what anything means, he instantly starts teaching as if we've already been learning discrete math structures and provides little help when questions are asked. Not a lot of homework, tests are in person.

Very boring class and lecture. Literally reads off a manuscript and then expects people to want to be interactive. Seemed nice though. Class was super easy. Stopped attending after 2 weeks because who wants to go to class at 7am to listen to someone read off a paper for an hour. Easy quizzes and easy papers. Just requires some time and effort.

After a few weeks, he told us to close our laptops since we didn't need them and just had to sit there and listen. So I stopped attending. 4 quizzes where you choose a side and explain, no right or wrong answer. 2 4-page papers, and a 10-page final paper. As long as you follow ALL the instructions, you should get a good grade.

The professor is very enthusiastic and passionate about the topics he discusses, the more questions asked the more entertaining of a lecture. Always sharing related articles so we are up to date. As a cs student the rf assignment was ok but don't procrastinate incase you have questions. Not sure how non cs people felt about.

Spring 2023 Entire class is based on group project & 1 multiple choice final. Groups are chosen by prof. It is fullstack project with either python/react with mysql. lecture was good went over lots of swe concepts. He grades based on milestones and number of github commits. Should really change the policy people commit unnecessary code to github.

I really enjoyed the mock-tech company experience. Professor Petkovic really cared a lot. We had a teammate who wasn't pulling his weight which made it a bit harder for the rest of us, make sure you know the people you pick for this class. Make sure to study for the final.

The most humble and smart Professor in the department! He has worked at huge tech companies and does research at Stanford, but still wants to make sure every student does well and enjoys and learns the software development life cycle. Semester long project to make a webapp. He doesn't care what languages you use, and loves growing the idea with you

Professor Petkovic is the best in the department and one of the best in the university! He gives 1 small homework, the final, and a group project! He makes you truly get better about good user experience and quality assurence and you be ready for industry after taking him! He responds fast to emails and gives a lot of extra credit!
Has worked in industry. Really cares.

He's hilarious and cover good topics of SW and HCI in general. But a good professor? NO. Why? Because putting in a random group with freeloaders who just sit and still receive grades put pressure on others who actually contribute. And what Petkovic response is "resolve with team first before bring up to me". What type of SW Management is that??????

The prof. was fine, but don't expect him to teach you coding. What really hurt the most was teaming up with people who don't want to participate and do the work. Just can't believe some cs seniors have no sense of responsibility whatsoever even though they are almost graduating. Having freeloaders in a team is just a BAD experience overall.
He is assigns a lot. There's a lot of work of to do in your group. He assumes because you're in a group that it will be easy and grade harshly on it. Only take if there's no other.

Great professor when it comes to giving you an idea of what a real software development environment will feel like working when working at a company. Consisted of semester-long project of developing a website with a team of 6-7 people as well as a final exam. That's it. Just show up to lecture and sit back, relax, and enjoy the show.

Can't wait to take the next 2 courses with Professor Ta! The only professor who is always positive and productive, even during this sad time at State U, despite continued destructive budget cuts and historic admission declines. His courses are still the best. He works super hard. He has a HUGE heart for his students, and he is a gifted educator.

Work hard, and you will find this professor the best. He cares that you learn and be ready for the demands in the workplace. Always start assignments early and pay attention during lecture. You will enjoy his teaching thoroughly. He is a natural and genuine educator. His materials are enormously useful.

Uses examples with mickey mouse. Idk what to tell you. its fun. Joke aside, he goes greatly in depth about things that other professors will just gloss over. Stuff professors would allocate 1 week to he does 2. He wants to make sure you actually understand how something works instead of just telling you how to use it.
He is the best computer science professor in SFSU. He gives you a lot of opportunities to boost your grade during the semester. His explanations are very clear.
He is the best professors I have ever taken in my life. He teaches really well and gives you a lot of opportunities to boost your grade.
The best educator in the entire history of education! TAKE HIM!!!

Funny guy, good at making lectures engaging. Great at explaining concepts in depth. For homework, though, ALWAYS start early. You will be crying if you don't. For 220, he scares you with a huge first assignment to weed out quitters. He ensures that he always goes at a pace that the whole class is comfortable with and will answer any questions.
My man. He makes learning so fun and effective. He is definitely the best.

Extremely lucky to have had him for my last 3 courses. I do not believe I will find a better professor than Professor Ta in my life. Extremely grateful. He is a gifted educator who works hard and loves his students. He genuinely cares and possesses endless patience. He is a gem at SFSU.

Professor Ta designed his courses thoroughly and properly. He makes proper adjustments along the way. This takes hard work, passion, experience, and a big heart. Not to mention his natural outstanding ability to teach so effectively, which by itself alone already sets him superior to any other professors at State U. Hats off.
He was disrespectful to me once and that's not something I ever tolerate. I confronted him about it and everything was cleared up, but he needs to watch his tone and attitude.
Great Professor and inspiring person

There will be 5 millstones for the group project, make sure to catch up, or else your group will be left behind. He is always available to answer your question and regrade, so keep trying to get your project become better. Presentation by the end of semester is very important, make sure all of your group members show up and perform well!
Very nice and understanding professor, but his zoom lecture is a bit boring.
Nice professor overall, he is very understanding and helpful. You will be assigned in a team of 6 people and working on 1 project for the whole semester.

The professor is unorganized in her lecture material; it is impossible to apply what is taught in class to your homework or tests. The textbook is $95 and will probably get more expensive. She posts no reviews or mock exams for you to practice for upcoming tests.

Lectures are not related to course content. Test materials are not covered in class, but only in the following homework assignment. Tests cover obscure syntax and badly worded questions, and the highest test grade rarely exceeds 80%, average test grade is less than 70%. Expensive zyBooks subscription required.
wort professor i have ever seen in my carrer

She knows the subject well, but that doesn't mean she's a good at teaching it. She speaks like were on the same intellectual level as her about C++. Just make sure to do ALL the assignments on ZyBooks and you will be fine. Quiz, midterm and final are worth a low percent. The assignments are worth like 50%. She at least lets you use GitHub Copilot
do not recommend

Her classes are really boring because she keeps talking to herself about anything and everything. And after all this, she has a WRITTEN CODING exam!! ALSO she made us pay $89 for zybooks (online reading assignments that we'd have 2 weeks to do with tons of in-built assignments). Overall, do not recommend this professor

Her projects are really hard and she created it those herself and half the time she doesn't even know how we coded it either. She takes 3-4 weeks to tell us how to use AI and then tells us not to use it for our assignments.
Hui Yang is the worst professor that we have taken so far. She is very set in her ways and will not be flexible with anything including deadlines. .

Lectures don't correlate with class or assignments most of the time. Uses Zybooks online text for reading assignments and labs with a poor autograder where you don't get points if you get one thing incorrectly. No extensions, no late work, and extremely hard to reach outside of class. 9 reading hws, 6 labs, 3 group projects, and occasional quizzes.

provided little to no clear instruction on what to expect on assignments that were outside of zybooks($89 sub that rarely ties into lectures). Her grading is inconsistent when brought up little to no dialogue is had. It is ironic she gives us a survey but does not listen to the fact most of us agree her instructions are unclear and rushed

Very passionate about Computer Graphics, their applications, and the industry. Nice person all around and helpful. However, lectures feel dull, tangents aren't uncommon, assignment windows are small (as in, 5 hours before it's due). Overall, good person but not so great teacher, you're better learning OpenGL on your own.
she does not teach no preparation for lecture no idea what she is talking about acts like she cares but doubtful no actions learned nothing from her but time wasting

Ilmi was amazing at CSCXXX and awful at other topics. Bad luck to take her and James Wong for foundation courses. They taught nothing. James was somewhat better than Ilimi to be fair. They ended computer science for me before it even started. Stay away from IImi.

She always claims she cares so deeply about her students but frequently her style of teaching is her way or the high way. She is not understanding if you miss quizzes or deadlines in general. Her TA's do most of the grading anyways so it's a luck of draw how you'll do that semester.

More interested in teaching/testing you on how a computer renders graphics than teaching you what you need to learn to make games. That you'll learn on your own. Multiple tests with math problems about how pixels are rendered--sorry but that is graphics, not game design. Also gave us math problems on quizzes that she never walked through completely
Doubtful she ever prepares for lectures. Disgusting she regularly demands acknowledgement.
Ilmi is increasingly inappropriate and irrelevant.

The most disorganized teacher I have ever had. In my opinion quite often did not know what she was talking about. Unclear instructions for multiple assignments. This wasn't just me, most of the people I knew in the class were annoyed by her coursework being so haphazard and disorganized. Didn't teach much, mostly surface level stuff.

Overall - a good experience. She sometimes assumes the students know a certain topic and goes over it quickly - It's important to interject and ask her to elaborate at these junctures. She's a good explainer though. Needs to be a bit more organized. Cares about students doing well.

They say it's an intro class but it's VERY HARD. 1 month in, she's ZOOMING through topics. You have 1 project due every week and 2 lectures for it. I can BARELY understand her during lectures. Midterm, quizzes, projects are badly phrased. We barely used the book. I got an A cause I went to tutoring. If you're fresh to coding, don't take her!

Professor Song is amazing and cares deeply about her students. For 648 the group project, she always checks in every week and provides helpful feedback. She is also incredibly talented and respected.Highly recommend

Probably the sweetest and kindest professor at SFSU. Professor Song is extremely knowledgeable as there's almost no question she cannot answer or assist with about software engineering. She cares so much about her students and their learning experience, giving you all the resources to succeed in this class. Take her if you can!!!

648 is based entirely on one group project, with Professor Song acting as a manager for each group. She is extremely helpful and kind to students who are struggling or ask for help. She provides lots of resources for students and makes sure that each member does their part. She DOES hold lazy students accountable.

Took her for 648. Entire course is a semester-long group project with the weekly lecture to guide development. You better work with your team or else you're not passing, and you have to TRY to fail because she's VERY generous. As long as you're putting in effort, you're passing the class

Very easy class. However if you are stuck with incompetent teammates then good luck because this class requires a lot of independent research. She does enforce people to participate otherwise you are getting a 0 for your final project, which is 70% of your grade. She gives extra credit by you showing up for class on time. Total of 7%!

Hard to understand, instead of her explaining topics she will have a student answer a question and reward them by having them teach lecture. Provides little to no help outside of class, reads off powerpoints. If you take her class be prepared to teach yourself.

Horrible. Absolutely horrible. For one, you can't understand her most of the time. Two, she has her TA do the grading. Since he's a student, he'll deduct full points for any error he finds. Three, she doesn't teach with heart but rather like it's a workout, as in she repeats the topic but doesn't say it any more clearly, giving a "phew" in the end.
So Ez

Professor Wong is spot-on with the power points. But when it comes to programming projects, it starts out pretty easy, as the semester goes on, it will begin to get harder. In terms of tests/quizzes, 1-2 quizzes and 2 tests (midterm and final exam). A Discussion Leader attendance is important for this class.

His teaching is just reading off powerpoints. Around 5 or 6 assignments, 2 midterms, and a final. The first few assignments are okay but it gets difficult later on. His midterms and finals are long and hard and he doesn't give enough time to take them. Don't take him if you don't know Java. If you do know Java, you should be able to pass.

Professor Wong's class was nicely organized, as it pretty much just followed the syllabus. Assignments are clear and are easy if you just follow along with the lectures. Lectures are a bit boring/Prof. Wong just reads off power points.

If this is your first time coding you'll struggle no matter what but James Wong lets you turn in assignments late the first half of the semester and really emphasizes learning how to code instead of focusing on your grade. Pretty good teacher.

He knows the material and his tests are very straightforward. His lectures do end up getting really boring after 20 minutes. I had relearn the material outside of class. His homework wouldn't make sense unless you know the material. Unless you are good at teaching yourself, I do not recommend this instructor.

Knowledgeable and nice professor with generous grading scale. He got some accent, but you will get use to it. He has an easy grading criteria. Attendance is free 10%, he dropped 2 lowest homework/quiz, gives partial credits on tests, willing to curve if average is below 75%, you can do 5% extra credits report, and final is pretty straightforward.

Professor Wong is clearly knowledgeable about algos and is fairly lenient when it comes to grades. His accent is heavy/lectures can be confusing because of course content. There are 2 exams, 6 hw, 1 coding assignment, participation, final, and extra credit report. Keep up with the hw/lectures and exams will be super easy.

His lectures are boring / will confuse you bc accent is thick. Since its a CS class just go on your laptop and read the textbook on the topic youre on so you dont get too far behind. Dr. Doolani is a new professor but is fair in her teaching and grading.

All material is from a powerpoint the pervious 220 teacher left. She didn't answer questions very well. Dropped my grade by 10% a week after finals were done and didnt respond to messages when questioned why.

I recently took CSC 510 with Professor Timothy Sun. The class structure includes 6 homeworks, with 2-3 weeks allotted to complete each one. I don't normally rate professors but professor Sun is an exception. Never have i thought i would enjoy learning and writing algorithms so much. VERY good at teaching CSC 510. Lectures aren't recorded but slides are uploaded and clear and concise to understand. Highly recommend if you're taking CSC 510.

Great professor, his lectures actually have coherence which is honestly rare for the CS department at SFSU. The material is difficult but I feel like Sun makes it easier with his teaching. Write notes on what he says, not as much on what he has on slides.

Timothy is a gentle professor on assignment, his explains ideas in algorithms clear and precisely. HWs are not that hard if you do study materials. This class should be harder, and you should learn more from this topic.
Amazing professor, very helpful, organized, lots of improvement opportunities. CSC 220 is a weeder class regardless of who you take. Just study and take advantage of the extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Bethel is an inspiration to students. His classes develop the skills it takes to succeed, both the hard knowledge and the soft skills, such as technical writing.
